A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AURC-estimation work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original estimator evaluations on CIFAR10/100, ImageNet, and Amazon Reviews, plus classifier fine-tuning results in Table 1.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical evaluations and fine-tuning results, including the extensive appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The two fixed-model plug-in estimators and fine-tuning objectives remain unchanged. New Appendix A.3 describes a limited Bayesian adaptation that averages AURC over the model posterior using Monte Carlo sampling; this extension is not experimentally evaluated.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-classification and review-rating tasks using CIFAR10/100, ImageNet, and Amazon Reviews. Bayesian models, distribution shift, and imbalanced datasets are discussed without adding evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The estimator comparisons retain SELE and 2×SELE, while Table 1 retains CE and SELE training comparisons. No comparison method is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Table S2 changes Negative Entropy from sum_i p_i log(p_i) to sum_i z_i log(z_i), although p denotes softmax probabilities and z denotes logits. This revises a reported evaluation setting without establishing an implementation change or rerun. Batch sizes, training budgets, learning rate, and other stated protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The sample-size and CSF sensitivity studies, comparisons across loss functions, bias/MAE/MSE analyses, and empirical AURC-equivalence check are retained. The new Bayesian discussion adds no ablation, robustness experiment, or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed fine-tuning aggregation, five-model analyses, batch-based uncertainty summaries, and two-sided t-test for AURC equivalence. No repeated-run count or statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All 48 mean-and-standard-deviation cells in Table 1 and the plotted contents of Figures 1–6 and S7–S28 match. The equivalence-test p-values remain 0.9981 and 0.998. No new empirical outcomes accompany the Bayesian extension.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 defines posterior-expected AURC and exchanges expectations using Fubini's theorem in Equations (37)–(38). V3 also replaces observation index i with rank r_i in the MSE and beta-distribution formulas, and changes Equation (1)'s accepted output from argmax classification to f(x). The central convergence guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution statements retain the population-AURC formulation, reweighted-risk interpretation, two consistent estimators, O(sqrt(ln(n)/n)) convergence rate, and suitability for fine-tuning. The Bayesian discussion is framed as an exploratory extension.

C2.justification: The expanded conclusion explicitly identifies fixed-model estimation as the main scope and distribution shift and imbalance as future work. Appendix A.3 adds discussion of posterior model uncertainty and possible connections to epistemic risk. Interpretations of existing experiments are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds a code-availability statement and an address for the authors' AsymptoticAURC repository, absent from v2. Existing training hyperparameters, model descriptions, and hardware information are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Cortes et al. (2016), Learning with Rejection, and Hendrickx et al. (2024), a reject-option survey, to the introduction and references. Other reference changes mainly update metadata for existing works; the central positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds an explanation of ascending ranks after Equation (12), expands the conclusion, inserts the Bayesian appendix subsection and an Impact Statement, and makes local wording, heading, and affiliation edits. Most prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The publication template changes typography, headers, and captions, with relocated figures and Table S2 and some appendix figures placed on separate pages. Existing plot panels and table structures are retained. Figure S7's subcaptions acquire inconsistent 'Figure S6' labels.

improvement.justification: V3 improves rank-dependent formulas, explains scope more explicitly, and supplies a code-access reference while retaining the empirical evidence. However, Table S2 replaces probability-based Negative Entropy with a raw-logit expression, creating a mathematical and reproducibility problem. The PDFs do not establish whether this is only a transcription error or reflects computation. These limited benefits and the unresolved error prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
